DISCUSSION

The more weight that is applied to a conveyor belt, the more the drive motor is loaded, thus decreasing speed. It would be costly for an operator to be present to monitor and vary the drive signal voltage every time the belt speed varied.eed varied...

Before designing an electronic means of controlling the closed loop system (conveyor belt), let's look at the responsibilities of the human controller. The operator and controlling circuitry perform four basic functions...

First, the operator must sense a change in speed of the conveyor belt. A tachometer would measure the number of revolutions a shaft turns in one minute and display the information on a meter for the human operator...

Second, the operator must make a decision about whether the belt is running too fast or too slow. Some comparison between a reference speed and the monitored speed must be known before corrective action is taken...

Third, the operator must increase or decrease the drive signal as needed to compensate for motor loading. The belt should never be loaded or unloaded to the point where the maximum or minimum drive signal cannot correct for the required speed...

Fourth, depending on the type of motor (AC or DC), several methods of motor control and feedback are available. DC motors are the most prevalent choice, because the AC motor is not easily varied because frequency, not amplitude is the major drive signal factor that determines speed...

For DC motors; the simplest, but least desirable method of speed control is a series rheostat. By adjusting the resistance in series with a DC motor, the voltage drop across the motor is changed which varies the speed. Series motors are ideal for applications that require large starting torque...
Depending upon cost and accuracy, Power transistors, Field Effect Transistors (FET) and TRIACs, and other semiconductor devices are the most efficient in controlling motor speed.

Transistor switching circuits can turn the current to the armature rapidly on and off. The current on time and off time are electronically varied to control motor speed. If the pulses are on longer than they are off, the motor runs faster...

With these steps in mind, an electronic controller can be designed to replace the human operator. Shaft RPM, accuracy, prime mover (AC or DC) motor and the total cost limits must all be considered in the decision...

In an electronic controlled closed loop system, the method of measuring shaft RPM will determine how accurate the system will be. The smallest change in speed must be detected and a signal produced that is capable of being easily processed...

DEFINITION
Photoelectric and magnetic transducers (sensors) are found in all areas of industrial controls. In selecting motor-source combinations, the DC prime mover should be the first consideration...
The use of DC motors in closed loop feedback systems has numerous advantages. Torque characteristics, universal supply voltage (AC or DC), and ease of speed control make it the preferred choice...
Electromagnetic Field Coils Allow AC/DC Operation

The universal DC motor can be powered by an AC or DC source. When AC is applied, the current and voltage polarity reversals are applied to both armature and the field coil at the same time. This allows the armature to continue rotating in the same direction...

Recall that if both armature and field polarities are reversed, than the direction of shaft rotation remains constant. If only the field or only the armature polarity is reversed, the direction of rotation reverses...

If AC is used as the source voltage, line current is also AC, and no rectification or filtering is necessary. Only step-up or step-down transformers are required, which keeps power supply design, construction, and cost to bare minimum...

The heart of any speed regulating circuit is the controller. An initial drive signal is applied to a motor having a certain load, which establishes a reference RPM. The RPM is compared to the feedback information to see if the drive signal should be altered...
